construction.shape: Short authentication string over an in-band agreement, committed before revealed, typed rather than compared
construction.commitment: SHA-256( LP("done/enroll-commit/v1") || LP(role) || LP(hex nonce) ), role in {existing, new}
construction.transcript: LP("done/enroll/v1") || LP(workspace_id) || LP(dec epoch) || LP(hex epoch_head) || LP(existing_credential_id) || LP(new_credential_id) || LP(hex new_wrapping_key) || LP(hex new_signing_key) || LP(hex recovery_state_digest) || LP(hex nonce_existing) || LP(hex nonce_new)
construction.epoch_head: Bound because row 9 asked for it. A device enrolling here is talking to one that already knows where the lineage is, so the typed symbols authenticate the head as well as the wrapping key — and row 9 never reaches this arrival path.
construction.new_signing_key: Bound because the successor’s member entry is (credential_id ‖ W_pub ‖ S_pub) and set approvals verify under member S_pub’s (P-1, ratified 2026-08-28): the SAS vouches for the signing key as well as the wrapping key.
construction.recovery_state_digest: SHA-256( LP("done/recovery-state/v1") || LP(dec counter) || LP(hex R_pub) || LP(hex recovery_envelope_digest) || LP(hex root_commitment) || LP(hex bootstrap_signer) ) — the recovery recipient the new device installs, inside what the typed symbols authenticate (TRD §§13.5/13.8). Its preimage is published in the honest vector’s inputs, so the digest — and therefore the transcript — reconstructs from published values alone (FU-05).
construction.transcript_hash: SHA-256(T). The ceremony’s identity, and what a wrap is bound to.
construction.sas: HKDF-SHA256(ikm = T, salt = "", info = LP("done/enroll-sas/v1"), L = 5); symbol i = ALPHABET[byte_i & 0x1f]
construction.alphabet: Crockford Base32: 0123456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ (no I, L, O, U) — row 14’s, reused
construction.entropy: 25 bits. One guess per admitted credential, not per attempt; see the selection document §4.
construction.direction: Displayed on the new device, typed into the existing one. The existing device is the one deciding whether to release a content key, so it is the one that must be given evidence.
construction.wrap_info: LP("done/enroll-wrap/v1") || LP(hex transcript_hash), as HPKE base-mode info
construction.length_prefix: uint16be(byteLength) || utf8 — injective, so no field can shift another
construction.nonce_caveat: Nonces are fixed inputs in these vectors so the composition is testable. Production generates 32 fresh bytes per side; the fixed nonce is not the discipline, the commitment is.

not_here.primitives: SHA-256, HKDF and X25519 KATs are row 1’s, in test/vectors/algorithm-suite.json.
not_here.wrap: The HPKE seal itself is row 1’s primitive and row 4’s framing. This row pins only its `info`.
not_here.admission: Admitting the new credential and signing the successor epoch is §13.6’s first gate, and rows 9 and 12.

new_device.role: The new device’s wrapping keypair. Its public half is what the SAS authenticates.

substituted.role: A key the service controls, offered in the new device’s place. §11.2 test 7’s attack, as a value.

new_device_signing.role: The new device’s Ed25519 signing credential. The successor’s member entry carries it, and set approvals verify under it — which is why the SAS must vouch for it.

substituted_signing.role: A signing key the service controls, offered in the new device’s place — the approval-authority half of §11.2 test 7’s attack.

vectors.name: honest-enrollment
vectors.why: A laptop enrolling a phone at epoch 9. Both sides derive this transcript and this string. Every transcript input is published here — FU-05 found recovery_state_digest inserted by generator internals only, so the artifact could not be independently reconstructed for its new load-bearing field.

grinding_demonstration.why: The reason the nonces are committed before they are revealed. A service that reveals second and is not committed can search its nonce until the string comes out as it likes.
grinding_demonstration.method: Candidate i is SHA-256("done/grind-demo" || uint32be(i)), so the count is a fact about the construction rather than about this run. The substituted wrapping key is in place throughout.
grinding_demonstration.extrapolation: Forcing all five symbols is the same search at 2^25 — seconds of work. The commitment is what makes 25 bits mean 25 bits.

must_fail.name: commitment-opened-with-wrong-nonce
must_fail.mutate: Reveal a nonce other than the one committed to. This is the whole point of the commit phase: whoever reveals second cannot choose.

must_fail.name: commitment-role-echoed
must_fail.mutate: Present the existing device’s commitment as the new device’s. Without `role` in the commitment the two are structurally identical and this succeeds.

must_fail.name: substituted-wrapping-key
must_fail.mutate: The service offers its own X25519 public key in the new device’s place. **This is §11.2 test 7**, and the SAS not matching is the whole of §13.6’s second gate.

must_fail.name: substituted-signing-key
must_fail.mutate: The service offers its own Ed25519 signing key in the new device’s place. The successor’s member entry is (credential_id ‖ W_pub ‖ S_pub) and set approvals verify under member S_pub’s (P-1, ratified 2026-08-28), so an unbound signing key would hand the service the approval authority the certified set exists to withhold from it — §11.2 test 7’s attack against the entry’s third field.

must_fail.name: wrong-workspace
must_fail.mutate: Run the ceremony against a different workspace id.

must_fail.name: wrong-epoch
must_fail.mutate: Replay the transcript under a later epoch. An authorization successor does not carry a completed ceremony forward with it.

must_fail.name: stale-epoch-head
must_fail.mutate: The current epoch number paired with the previous epoch’s head — what a service feeds a new device that has no history of its own. **This is row 9 discharged through the person**: the existing device knows where the lineage is, so the five symbols disagree.

must_fail.name: wrong-existing-credential
must_fail.mutate: Name a different existing device as the one releasing the key.

must_fail.name: wrong-new-credential
must_fail.mutate: Name a different credential as the one enrolling. The credential id is minted per enrollment, so this is what stops a whole ceremony being replayed.

must_fail.name: wrong-existing-nonce
must_fail.mutate: Substitute the existing device’s revealed nonce.

must_fail.name: wrong-new-nonce
must_fail.mutate: Substitute the new device’s revealed nonce.

must_fail.name: transposed-nonces
must_fail.mutate: Exchange the two nonces. The transcript binds them in fixed positions, so the ceremony is role-ordered and swapping the devices is a different ceremony.

must_fail.name: substituted-recovery-state
must_fail.why: The wrapping-key substitution one carrier along, and the one the transcript could not see. The service admits the genuine new device, authenticates its genuine W_pub, and hands it an attacker-controlled R_pub with a matching opaque envelope. Every symbol of the SAS matches, the enrollment succeeds, and the honestly-enrolled device wraps every future generation to a key the service holds. Binding the recovery state the new device installs is what makes the existing device unable to certify a recipient it does not itself hold.

must_fail.name: aad-only-renumbered-transcript-label
must_fail.mutate: Derive the SAS under "done/enroll/v2". The label is where this carrier authenticates its own version (row 1).
